summary: Microsoft switches AI capability and spend on by default in the next ten weeks: Claude in Swiss and EU tenants on 9 December, metered Copilot experiences from January, pay-as-you-go Copilot Business billing in Q1 2027. Decide every default before its date, with a named owner.
tradeoff: In the next ten weeks Microsoft switches AI capability and spend on by default. Claude models go live for all users in Swiss and EU tenants on 9 December unless an admin opts out. Metered Cowork, Code and Autopilot become visible to every licensed user from the end of January. Usage-based billing turns on by default for new Copilot Business orders in Q1 2027, capped at 4,000 Copilot Credits per user per month. Copilot Chat limits already nudge unlicensed staff to request or buy seats. Accepting the defaults speeds adoption, but spreads a new AI subprocessor, a consumption bill and more non-human identities across the tenant without anyone having decided.

Do we let vendor defaults set the pace and monitor after the fact, or opt out across the board and accept that blocked demand moves to shadow AI? DNSFilter reports that 20.1% of organisations have already had a security incident from an unapproved AI connection.

Decide every default before its date, with a named owner: enable, scope to groups, or switch off. Scope Claude to specific groups by 9 December, set Copilot spending limits below the 4,000-credit default before the next order, allow access requests for metered experiences by role, and move third-party AI apps to admin consent. Opt in by decision, not by default.

pillars.name: Financial & Licensing Realities
pillars.subtitle: Seats become seats plus a meter
pillars.reality: From 1 December, Copilot can be bought without a Microsoft 365 base licence, and new SKU IDs replace the '(add-on)' offers for new purchases. In Q1 2027, new Copilot Business orders through CSP switch on pay-as-you-go by default, and one new order also turns metering on for the Copilot Business licences you already have. Analysts meanwhile estimate that about one in three paid Copilot seats goes unused in a typical week.
pillars.action: Set tenant spending limits and alerts below the 4,000-credit default before the next Copilot Business order, and ask your CSP for the go-live date. Reclaim seats idle for 28 days or more before renewal, and update quote templates and software asset management rules for the new SKU IDs.

pillars.name: Governance & Data Hygiene
pillars.subtitle: Every AI path needs an owner
pillars.reality: Three new paths into company data open at once. Claude becomes a Microsoft subprocessor in everyday use on 9 December. Agent identities sit outside Conditional Access policies aimed at 'all users', and idle ones will be disabled after 60 days by a new default policy. And employees grant third-party AI tools OAuth access: 43% of organisations only find out afterwards, or never.
pillars.action: Legal and Security record the Anthropic choice before 9 December and update the record of processing activities. Inventory agent identities, give each a human sponsor, and add agent-targeted Conditional Access in report-only mode first. Switch Entra to the admin consent workflow for third-party apps.

pillars.name: Digital Employee Experience
pillars.subtitle: Patch regressions and sign-in changes hit the helpdesk
pillars.reality: The November Windows updates can fail to print documents with invisible zero-size images (watermarks, generated templates), broke KMS activation scripts until the 13 November out-of-band fix, and October's LDAP hardening can cut access to some NetApp SMB shares. Admins report NTLM signing breaking App Volumes in VDI. Some SMS and voice MFA sign-ins now show a CAPTCHA, and cross-tenant calendars with partners break unless moved off EWS.
pillars.action: Keep the security update deployed. Have template owners in Finance, Legal and HR test print-critical documents this week, and start the NTLM signing audit well before May 2027. Prepare helpdesk scripts for the MFA CAPTCHA and Copilot Chat limits, and migrate cross-tenant calendar sharing after 23 November together with partner admins.

pillars.name: Culture, Adoption & Change Velocity
pillars.subtitle: Measure pull, not push
pillars.reality: Licences assigned are not adoption: about a third of paid seats sit idle in a typical week. At the same time, Copilot Chat limit prompts and the new 'Request access' buttons will create a stream of bottom-up demand, and blocking without an approved alternative pushes staff towards unapproved tools.
pillars.action: Treat licence and access requests as the demand signal. Route them through one approval path that asks which business process the seat will speed up, point 'Learn more' to internal guidance with champion examples, and publish an HR-owned acceptable-use policy that names the approved tools. Report time saved in named processes, not licences assigned.

calls: Agree the Anthropic setting before 9 December, confirm every agent identity has a sponsor and agent-targeted Conditional Access, and choose the SMS and voice MFA path before 1 February 2027.

Set Copilot spending limits below the 4,000-credit default before the next Copilot Business order, plan the 1 December SKU change and the renewal seat audit, and budget a telephony provider if SMS MFA stays.

Confirm print-critical templates work on the November build, the out-of-band fix is in the images, the NTLM signing audit has started, and helpdesk scripts are ready for the MFA CAPTCHA and Copilot Chat limits.
antipattern_head: Stop letting default settings and upgrade prompts make your AI decisions.
antipattern_body: This quarter, Microsoft's defaults decide who gets Claude, who sees metered agents and when consumption billing starts, while Chat limit prompts push staff to ask for seats. Buying seats in response to prompts, or leaving defaults untouched because nobody owns them, produces shelfware and unbudgeted consumption at the same time. Every default on the cliff list below needs a named owner and a recorded choice before its date.

items.title: Claude models switch on by default for EU and EFTA Copilot tenants
items.sowhat: Swiss and EU tenants that never made a choice get Anthropic's Claude models for all users across Copilot and Copilot Studio, with processing moving into the EU Data Boundary. The 'Microsoft 365 apps only' option is retired and moves to All users.
items.action: Choose All users, Specific users and groups, or No users this week under Copilot > Settings > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Anthropic; update the record of processing activities.

items.title: Copilot Business pay-as-you-go billing switches on by default in CSP
items.deadline: Jan to Mar 2027, no day set
items.sowhat: A new Copilot Business purchase through a CSP partner turns on usage-based billing by default, capped at 4,000 Copilot Credits per user per month, and also turns on metering for the Copilot Business licences already in the tenant.
items.action: Ask the CSP partner for your go-live date; set a tenant spending limit below the default, with alerts, before the next order; agree who approves raising it.

items.title: SMS and voice MFA: CAPTCHA prompts now, Microsoft-provided delivery retires
items.sowhat: Some SMS and voice MFA attempts now need a CAPTCHA, and users behind restrictive proxies may fail to sign in. From 1 February 2027 Microsoft stops delivering SMS and voice itself: contract a telephony provider (Soprano, Telesign or Infobip) or move users to passkeys or Authenticator.
items.action: Count users still on SMS or voice; brief the helpdesk; decide in December between migration and a provider contract.

items.title: Copilot sold without a Microsoft 365 base licence; add-on offers end of sale in CSP
items.sowhat: New SKUs at the same price replace the '(add-on)' offers for new purchases; existing subscriptions keep renewing. Quotes, scripts and reports that match on offer names change, just as analysts estimate about one in three paid seats goes unused in a typical week.
items.action: Reclaim seats idle for 28 days or more before renewal; update quote templates and asset management rules for the new SKU IDs; buy standalone seats only for a named use case.

items.title: Copilot Cowork, Code and Autopilot become visible to every licensed user
items.sowhat: Licensed users will see metered experiences with a 'Request access' option even where they are not enabled. Without a rule, IT fields a request queue and nobody owns who may spend Copilot Credits.
items.action: Configure 'Access requests to usage-based billing experiences' by role (available from mid-November); from mid-December point 'Learn more' to internal guidance.

items.title: Unpublished Copilot Chat limits now hit users without a Copilot licence
items.sowhat: Since 2 November (up to 2,000 seats) and 9 November (larger tenants), unlicensed staff hit Chat limits that admins cannot see or adjust, and the notice nudges them to request or buy a licence.
items.action: Give the helpdesk a standard answer; turn off Copilot self-service purchase; route licence requests through one approval path with Procurement.

items.title: AI agent identities get lifecycle guardrails; 'all users' Conditional Access misses agents
items.sowhat: A default inactivity policy (preview, all tenants) notifies owners after 60 days and disables idle agent identities. Policies aimed at all users do not include agent user accounts, so agents can sit outside controls leaders assume cover everyone.
items.action: Inventory agents and give each a human sponsor; protect seasonal agents from the 60-day rule; add agent-targeted Conditional Access in report-only mode first.

items.title: One in five organisations report an incident from an unapproved AI connection
items.sowhat: In DNSFilter's survey of 400 IT and security managers (3 Nov), 20.1% had an incident from an unapproved AI connection, 43% only learn after the fact, or never, when an AI tool gets OAuth or API access, and 40.3% put their next security budget into AI governance.
items.action: Move Entra to the admin consent workflow; publish an HR-owned acceptable-use policy that names the approved AI tools.

items.title: November Windows updates break some printing, KMS activation and NetApp or VDI workflows
items.sowhat: Documents with invisible zero-size images may not print; KMS scripts failed until the 13 November out-of-band fix; LDAP hardening can cut NetApp SMB access; admins report NTLM signing breaking App Volumes in VDI.
items.action: Keep the update deployed; have owners of invoice, contract and payslip templates test printing this week; start the NTLM signing audit (events 4022 and 4023).

items.title: Cross-tenant free/busy and calendar sharing must move off Exchange Web Services
items.sowhat: Free/busy, MailTips and calendar sharing with partner organisations break unless moved to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy; the EWS extension lasts only until the final shutdown on 1 April 2027.
items.action: Run the affected-tenant checks; list dependent suppliers and subsidiaries; migrate with their admins once the 23 November rollout lands.

discarded: Release Planner retirement, the legacy Teams GitHub app, the Outlook usage report leaving the Exchange admin centre, Defender for Identity classic alert retirement, Word legacy compatibility settings, Teams mobile and Queues features, self-healing KB5132061 install loops, Partner Center sandbox renames, and January 2027 currency changes (AUD, CNY, INR, NOK and NZD only; no CHF or EUR change). Routine admin work with no strategic trade-off.
method: Signals from 2 to 16 November 2026 across Message Center, Partner Center, Entra and security advisories, admin community reporting and analyst research, kept only if they move budget, open a risk or governance gap, or create friction that needs IT, HR, Security, Procurement, Finance or Legal to align. Message Center items link to the public mirror at mc.merill.net. First Page Sage and DNSFilter figures are their own estimates and survey results.
